headline: Iran may 'initiate' attack before US strikes rather than wait past Nov 3

sources: Jonathan Schanzer, executive director, Foundation for Defense of Democracies, via Al Jazeera liveblog 13:15 GMT (17:15 )
fault_line: Strike first or wait: if Tehran believes the post-midterm bombing campaign is locked in, does waiting only hand Washington the initiative?

sections.what_happened: [ANALYSIS - scenario, not fact] Schanzer argues Tehran could launch a preemptive strike if its leaders believe US strikes are imminent, rather than wait until after the Nov 3 midterms: 'Why would they wait until after the elections here ... if they could initiate it and potentially gain the upper hand?' Context in the same entry: Trump may be looking at a post-Nov 3 timeline for action; the war has weighed on Republican candidates as US voters tire of rising gasoline prices; Pentagon estimate of the war's cost to US taxpayers is $47.1bn.
sections.what_verified: Single analyst's scenario via one liveblog family; no Iranian statement of preemptive intent retrieved in-window. Reported as analysis only.
sections.what_disputed: No Iranian preemptive-strike signal in-window; Araghchi's parallel track is mediation (seven-day Hormuz plan); Vance's letter to Rezaei (WSJ) points to a diplomatic off-ramp, not an Iranian first strike.
